about: ZEUS Lab registry (tools/zeus_lab.py, docs/ZEUS_LAB.md). Every candidate change for Zlarior (LIT) and ATLAS, written down BEFORE it is judged. Kinds: lit_tilt / atlas_tilt (size rule, engine/learn_loop rule language: first matching step sets the size x0-1.5, 0 = skip), lit_x (a tools/lit_edge management variant), parked (not built / another family: shown, never run). rejected_forever = the 'Tested and rejected' list: never run again; 'blocks' stops any experiment (cross ones included) on that bot + feature. The Lab NEVER edits live_model*.json, second_model.json or data/account_b.json; adoption = owner yes, then Claude runs the CLAUDE.md steps.

experiments.title: ATLAS: skip days when VIX closed under 15
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS takes no trade on a day whose prior VIX close is under 15 (calm days, small VIX-band targets). Today it trades them.
experiments.hypothesis: ATLAS's VIX-band targets shrink in a calm market; VIX < 15 lost R in every span in the revive diagnosis. Post-hoc (found by looking at Jul-Oct) and a knife edge (15.5 / 16 swing), so it must pass the full proof here.

experiments.title: ATLAS: x1.25 size when VIX closed at 18 or more
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS risks 25% more on days whose prior VIX close is 18 or higher. Other days unchanged.
experiments.hypothesis: VIX 18-22 was ATLAS's best bucket in Jan-Jun, Jul-Aug and 2021-24 (bigger VIX-band targets, same hit rate).

experiments.title: ATLAS: x1.25 size when the stop is tight vs the 5m ATR (bottom third)
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS risks 25% more when its stop is small next to the recent 5-minute candle size. Other trades unchanged.
experiments.hypothesis: A tight structural stop vs volatility = a clean level; the same $ risk buys more points of target. Different from the rejected 'stop > 1.6x the member's median' cut (that compared a member with itself, this compares with the market).

experiments.title: Zlarior: x1.25 size when the planned reward is big (R:R top third)
experiments.what_changes: Zlarior risks 25% more when its VIX-band target is far away compared with its stop. Other trades unchanged.
experiments.hypothesis: A far target on a tight stop is where the 8R bank pays. The tested idea was SKIPPING small-R:R trades (planned target < 6-7R, rejected); a size-up on the big ones was not tested.

experiments.title: Zlarior: from 14:00 ET the target is at most 3R
experiments.what_changes: A Zlarior trade entered at or after 14:00 ET aims for at most 3x its risk instead of the full VIX band (less time left in the day).
experiments.hypothesis: Late entries rarely reach a far target before the 15:55 flat; a nearer target banks them. Thin lead (2+1 trades) in the edge night.

experiments.title: Kalshi rewards: pause both quotes for an hour after a 5c move
experiments.what_changes: The Kalshi rewards quoter would stop quoting for an hour after the price jumps 5 cents (news, a score).
experiments.hypothesis: Fills after a jump are the losing ones; the pause helped in both halves pooled.
experiments.parked_why: Separate family (Kalshi, paused by the owner). Its own paper test (tools/kalshi_rewards_paper.py, GET only) is the shadow; no futures backtest applies.

experiments.title: Asia slot (18:00-02:00) at $300 a trade on the Rapid EOD
experiments.what_changes: A third lane on the Rapid account: Zlarior's setups in the Asia session at a fixed $300 risk.
experiments.hypothesis: A small plus in both 2026 halves ($5,133 / $3,035 vs $5,022 / $2,301 a month) but worse in 2021-25.
experiments.parked_why: Not built: the PC bot does not route Asia trades today, and 2021-25 is worse (2-week fails 4.7% vs 2.9%).

experiments.title: Zlarior: scale-in adds on the eval only from eval session 5
experiments.what_changes: After break-even Zlarior adds 1 micro, only on an eval and only from its 5th session; never on funded accounts.
experiments.hypothesis: Eval +$38.7k / +$24.9k vs +$34.8k / +$16.3k, 2-week pass up in both halves.
experiments.parked_why: Needs new code (lit_sizing scale_in_from_session in engine/live.py) and the owner's Sim101 round-trip proof first.

experiments.title: Zlarior: 15-minute structure trail after +1R
experiments.what_changes: Once a trade is +1R, the stop follows the 15-minute protected swing.
experiments.hypothesis: H1 +$467 / H2 +$13 at the LIT size, eval +$1,019 / +$3,762, one more 2-week fail in H1.
experiments.parked_why: Needs the structure engine in the Lab runner; the live advisor's trail_15m tally already watches it on real trades.

experiments.title: ATLAS: add the hunts x0.5 + the noise-area day-hold x0.5 as members
experiments.what_changes: Two more ATLAS members at half size.
experiments.hypothesis: More passes a month in all four spans.
experiments.parked_why: Fails the Jan-Jun 2-week test (62.2 / 5.9 vs 65.5 / 0.8) and 5-6 trades a week (rule: 2-4). Paper lead only.

experiments.title: ATLAS: new member - VWAP pullback with trend
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS gets a 4th member: buy the first dip to VWAP in an up-trend (sell the first rally in a down-trend), 10:00-14:30, stop 1 tick beyond the last 3 bars, one target.
experiments.hypothesis: On a trending RTH morning the first dip to the session VWAP that closes back on the trend side is where late traders re-enter (VWAP rising over 30 min; s1 also needs the move from the open >= 0.5 x the 14-day sigma).

experiments.title: ATLAS: new member - Opening-drive continuation (1m trigger)
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS gets a 4th member: after a strong opening drive, enter the pullback's 1m turn in the drive's direction, until 11:00, stop 1 tick beyond the pullback, one target.
experiments.hypothesis: A strong 09:30 drive that pulls back 25-62% resumes; a 1m close beyond the last 3 1m extremes is the trigger (2026 on 1m; 2021-25 the same rule on 5m bars).

experiments.title: ATLAS: new member - Prior-day value-area re-entry (80% rule, re-measure)
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS gets a 4th member: Dalton's 80% rule (open outside yesterday's value area, back inside -> trade to the far edge).
experiments.hypothesis: Dalton's 80% rule (already rejected alone in the new-strategy hunt) re-measured once as an ATLAS member.

experiments.title: ATLAS: new member - 15m Keltner squeeze release
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS gets a 4th member: trade the first 15m close out of a Keltner squeeze box, stop beyond the breakout bar or box middle, one target.
experiments.hypothesis: Bollinger(20, 2) inside Keltner(20, 1.5 ATR) for >= N 15m bars = compression; the first 15m close beyond the squeeze box within 3 bars of the release starts the move.

experiments.title: ATLAS: new member - Prior-day POC first touch (own idea)
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS gets a 4th member: fade the first touch of yesterday's point of control, stop 1 tick beyond the touch bar.
experiments.hypothesis: The prior RTH session's point of control holds the first time price trades back to it (own idea).

experiments.title: Zlarior: time stop - out after 60 minutes if the trade never reached +1R
experiments.what_changes: 60 minutes after the fill, a Zlarior trade that has not once been +1R (so no breakeven yet) is closed at the next 1-minute open. Today it waits for its stop, breakeven, target or 15:55.
experiments.hypothesis: Losers die slowly (median 42-44 min to the stop); a trade with no +1R in an hour is mostly a loser. Different from the 15-minute check (loss condition at minute 15 only) and the rejected slow-trade nearer target (kept the trade open).

experiments.title: Zlarior: out before the NY open if not yet at breakeven
experiments.what_changes: A trade filled before 09:29 ET that is still open and not at breakeven is closed at 09:29 (the 09:28 close decides). Trades already at breakeven run on.
experiments.hypothesis: 95 of 120 trades are London-morning trades; the 09:30 open is a new volatility regime that runs unprotected London trades through their stops. Exits by clock were never tested (only entry windows).

experiments.title: Zlarior: breakeven before the NY open when +0.5R or better
experiments.what_changes: At 09:29 ET a trade filled earlier, not yet at breakeven but at least +0.5R in profit, gets its stop moved to breakeven (+1.25 pts). Losing trades unchanged.
experiments.hypothesis: Protects London winners from the opening whip without cutting the ones still under water. BE at 0.75 / 0.9R at any time was rejected; this is a once-a-day clock rule.

experiments.title: Zlarior: out 2 minutes before big US news if not yet at breakeven
experiments.what_changes: An open trade not yet at breakeven is closed 2 minutes before a high-impact release (CPI, jobs, PPI 08:30; FOMC 14:00). At breakeven it runs on.
experiments.hypothesis: A release is a coin flip on a trade that has not worked yet; the old engine closed before news, LIT never did. The tested news rules were size / skip on news days, not an exit.

experiments.title: Zlarior: breakeven 2 minutes before big US news when +0.5R or better
experiments.what_changes: 2 minutes before a high-impact release, a trade at least +0.5R in profit but not yet at breakeven gets its stop moved to breakeven (+1.25 pts).
experiments.hypothesis: Keeps the news spike's upside, removes the chance a profitable trade turns into a full loss on the release.

experiments.title: Zlarior: after breakeven, out when 60 minutes pass without a new best price
experiments.what_changes: Once a trade is at breakeven, if 60 minutes pass without a new high (low for shorts) it is closed at the next 1-minute open instead of waiting for breakeven or the target.
experiments.hypothesis: The 34 breakevens went a median +1.85R before coming back; a stalled trade banks part of that. Not a trail (no stop moves) and not a giveback rule (time-based).

experiments.title: Zlarior: breakeven only after a 1-minute CLOSE at +1R (not the first touch)
experiments.what_changes: The stop moves to breakeven (+1.25 pts) when a 1-minute candle closes at +1R or better, instead of the first wick that touches +1R.
experiments.hypothesis: A wick to +1R that is sold at once is a weak touch; waiting for the close keeps fewer weak breakevens. Tested BE changes were later R levels, ATR / points triggers and structure closes, not a plain close at 1R.

experiments.title: Zlarior: x1.25 size the day after an NR7 (narrowest range of 7 sessions)
experiments.what_changes: When yesterday's session range was the smallest of the last 7 sessions, Zlarior risks 25% more on today's trade. Other days unchanged.
experiments.hypothesis: Range compression precedes expansion (Crabel NR7), and Zlarior's VIX-band targets need a day that travels. NR7 was tested only as a stand-alone strategy (public strategies 2026-11-17), never as a Zlarior size rule.

experiments.title: Zlarior: x1.25 size on London build-up sweeps (equal highs / lows, 02:00-08:00)
experiments.what_changes: When the swept level is a build-up (equal highs or lows) and the entry is in London (02:00-08:00 ET), Zlarior risks 25% more. Other trades unchanged.
experiments.hypothesis: The owner's A+ idea: build-ups are the cleanest engineered liquidity and London is where Zlarior earns. Sessions and level types were tested one at a time, never this pair as a size rule.

experiments.title: Zlarior: x0.75 size when the 18:00 open gapped against the trade
experiments.what_changes: When the session opened (18:00) away from the prior close against the trade's direction (bottom quarter of Jan-Jun gaps, in daily ATR), Zlarior risks 25% less.
experiments.hypothesis: An overnight gap against the trade is fresh order flow the other way; the sweep fights it. The overnight-gap context was never a Zlarior rule (premium/discount vs the 18:00 open was a skip, a different fact).

experiments.title: Zlarior: ATLAS's zombie-eval rule on the evals (1-micro last bullet at 80% of the room, give up under $200)
experiments.what_changes: When 40% of the eval's room is too small for even 1 micro, Zlarior takes 1 micro if a full stop-out fits 80% of the room (the soft daily loss still applies); an eval with less than $200 of room is given up and a fresh one bought. The trades and the funded size do not change.
experiments.hypothesis: ATLAS's one keeper (owner yes, 'Fix atlas'), never tried on Zlarior: low-room evals sit idle (the 25K #2 skips 21-31% of Zlarior's signals for lack of room) instead of passing or failing. Cross-learning ATLAS -> Zlarior.

experiments.title: Zlarior: the 50K and the 25K evals alternate full / half size on each signal
experiments.what_changes: On every 2nd Zlarior signal the 50K eval takes half its normal size and the 25K its full size, on the others the other way round, so one losing day never hits both evals at full size. The Lab scores the 50K's side; both evals together: tools/money/lit_two_evals.py.
experiments.hypothesis: The owner's two evals trade the same signals, so a losing streak hits both at once. Staggered START dates were tested (eval-game, lit-risk-money); staggered SIZING on two live evals never was.

experiments.title: ATLAS funded 25K: pause a member while its own last 10 / 20 trades lose (PF under 1)
experiments.what_changes: A member whose own last 10 or 20 paper trades have a profit factor under 1 trades 0 micros (or half) on the funded 25K until its record is back at PF 1; it keeps trading on paper meanwhile.
experiments.hypothesis: A member that has gone cold stays cold for a while, so pausing it keeps funded money.

experiments.title: ATLAS funded 25K: smaller size while ATLAS's edge light is AMBER / RED
experiments.what_changes: The funded 25K trades x0.75 / x0.5 / paper while ATLAS's own last-40-session light (tools/edge_health) is AMBER or RED, or its last-40 R-PF is under 1.5.
experiments.hypothesis: A weak last 40 sessions means weaker next weeks, so trading smaller then protects the account.

experiments.title: ATLAS funded 25K: a daily loss cap tied to the $1,100 buffer
experiments.what_changes: On the funded 25K ATLAS stops for the day after a losing trade, or caps the day's loss at $275 / $367 / a third of the room (today: $600 soft daily loss, max 2 trades).
experiments.hypothesis: A second loss on a bad day is what drains a small funded account; capping the day keeps the room for the next good trade.
experiments.pick: D4 day cap 1/3 of the room

experiments.title: ATLAS funded 25K: risk 30-50% of the room instead of 60% (in a hole, or always)
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS risks 40% / 30% of the room to the floor instead of 60% while the funded 25K is under its start balance, or 40% always (post-hoc: 50% always, 40% while under its best day-end balance).
experiments.hypothesis: Smaller bets make a string of losses less likely to strand the account under $100 of room (the bot then stops).

experiments.title: ATLAS funded 25K: skip calm days (VIX under 15) or the day after a losing day
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS takes no trade on the funded 25K on days whose prior VIX close is under 15 (re-measure), or on the session after a losing day.
experiments.hypothesis: Calm days shrink the VIX-band targets; a losing day is often followed by another.
experiments.pick: K2 skip the day after a losing day

experiments.title: Zlarior: x1.25 size on a pullback in the daily trend (daily trend with the trade, 1h trend against)
experiments.what_changes: Zlarior trades 25% bigger when yesterday's close is on the trade's side of its 20-day average AND the 1h trend (EMA 20 vs 50) points the other way: a dip in an uptrend or a rally in a downtrend (the classic triple-screen pullback). Everything else as today.
experiments.hypothesis: Win/loss anatomy: these trades made +1.35R / +1.74R / +0.22R a trade (Jan-Jun / Jul-Oct / 2021-25) vs +0.85R / +0.74R / +0.01R for all trades; the best of the 4 daily x 1h cells in Jan-Jun. Related family already rejected: the 1h structure-trend SKIP (structure-management.md); this is a size-up, never a skip.

experiments.title: Zlarior: skip what a careful human would skip (against both trends, late, news within 30 min, no room)
experiments.what_changes: No Zlarior trade when any of the 4 checklist flags is on: against the daily AND the 1h trend; the day already moved 1 daily ATR before the entry; a high-impact US release within 30 minutes after the entry; the prior-day high / low less than 1R ahead on the target side.
experiments.hypothesis: The owner's question: would skipping the trades a careful human skips have helped? The checklist was written before the first run (classic discretionary rules).

experiments.title: ATLAS: x1.25 size on London-open-hour entries (03:00-03:59 ET)
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS trades 25% bigger when the entry is in the 03:00 ET hour (08:00 London, the London open).
experiments.hypothesis: Win/loss anatomy: 03:00 entries made +1.99R / +1.61R / +0.32R a trade (Jan-Jun / Jul-Oct / 2021-25) vs +0.92R / +0.65R / +0.05R for all ATLAS trades (atlas_deep autopsy: '03:00 makes most of the money'). Window SKIPS were rejected (atlas-windows-entries-2026-10-30.md); this is a size-up of the best hour.

experiments.title: ATLAS: skip what a careful human would skip (against both trends, late, news within 30 min, no room)
experiments.what_changes: No ATLAS trade when any of the 4 checklist flags is on (the same checklist as for Zlarior); the slot stays free for a later ATLAS signal that day.
experiments.hypothesis: The owner's question, on ATLAS: the checklist was written before the first run.

experiments.title: Zlarior: human setup grade - skip C setups (more warnings than a typical setup)
experiments.what_changes: Before each Zlarior setup, count 7 human warnings (trend against, a level within half a stop, day already extended, inside day, news in 30 min, ES against, VIX not normal); skip the setup when it has more warnings than a typical one (3+ of 7), the day stays free for a later setup.
experiments.hypothesis: A calm discretionary trader passes on setups where several things are against him at once (higher-timeframe trend, a level in the way, a spent day, chop, news, ES, an abnormal VIX), without ever looking at his last result.

experiments.title: ATLAS: human setup grade - skip C setups (more warnings than a typical setup)
experiments.what_changes: Before each ATLAS signal, count the same 7 human warnings; skip the signal when it has more warnings than a typical one (3+ of 7), the slot stays free for the next signal.
experiments.hypothesis: A calm discretionary trader passes on setups where several things are against him at once (higher-timeframe trend, a level in the way, a spent day, chop, news, ES, an abnormal VIX), without ever looking at his last result.

experiments.title: Third strategy: Post-close move into the 18:00 reopen (follow / fade)
experiments.what_changes: A third strategy (own paper account): after a big post-close move, trade the 18:00 reopen with it or against it, stop beyond the move, out by 09:25 or 15:55.
experiments.hypothesis: A big 16:00 -> 17:00 move (mega-cap earnings hour, MFFU flat) keeps going (follow) or gives part back (fade) after the 18:00 reopen.

experiments.title: Third strategy: Camarilla / floor-trader pivots (RTH)
experiments.what_changes: A third strategy (own paper account): trade the classic Camarilla / floor pivots in NY hours, one a day.
experiments.hypothesis: Camarilla H3/L3 probes that close back inside fade, H4/L4 closes break out; floor R1/S1 probes fade to P.

experiments.title: Third strategy: TD Sequential 9-count exhaustion fade (15m / 1h, 24h)
experiments.what_changes: A third strategy (own paper account): fade a completed TD Sequential 9-count, any hour 18:00-15:30, one a day.
experiments.hypothesis: A completed TD Sequential 9-count (15m / 1h, whole CME day) marks exhaustion: fade it to 1R / 2R / bar 1.

experiments.title: Zlarior: cap the entry slippage (a limit order at most 2 ticks past the signal price)
experiments.what_changes: Zlarior would send its entry as a limit order at most 2 ticks past the signal price and skip the trade if it is not filled within 10 seconds.
experiments.hypothesis: Untested idea (bot-gap research, NinjaTrader / TradersPost execution controls): fewer bad fills, but it may skip fast winners.
experiments.parked_why: Untested idea, not built: it needs the PC's measured fills (engine/fill_audit) to size the cap and a backtest of skipped fast entries first.

experiments.title: Zlarior: size each trade with the measured slippage instead of a fixed 1 tick
experiments.what_changes: The sizer would price the median slippage of the last 10 real fills instead of a fixed 1 tick, so a planned risk stays the real risk after costs.
experiments.hypothesis: Untested idea (QuantConnect LEAN fill models): the $ at risk matches the plan more closely when fills slip more than 1 tick.
experiments.parked_why: Untested idea, not built: too few real fills yet (2 since Nov 16) to measure the slippage; a sizing change needs the CLAUDE.md proof first.

experiments.title: ATLAS: size each trade with the measured slippage instead of a fixed 1 tick
experiments.what_changes: ATLAS's $250 a trade would include the median slippage of its last 10 real fills, so a stop-out costs $250 and not more.
experiments.hypothesis: Untested idea (QuantConnect LEAN fill models): the real loss per stop matches the plan on the funded account.
experiments.parked_why: Untested idea, not built: ATLAS has 1 real fill so far; a sizing change needs the CLAUDE.md proof first.
